title: Mosaic starter templates: compact cross-lang LLM examples (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI)
creator: Ethan Moore
description: Goal: Ship a compact, opinionated starter kit (Mosaic) with language-specific examples that show idiomatic usage of Redwood SDKs for streaming, retry/backoff, observability, and production readiness. The deliverable will be four runnable minimal apps + short cookbook snippets: 1) Next.js streaming SSR chat widget with resumable streams and token-level cost breakdown hooks; 2) FastAPI async inference gateway that demonstrates background prewarming, request-level retries with idempotency keys, and KV-prefix caching; 3) Go HTTP server using http.Flusher for chunked streaming, connection pooling for long-lived connections, and graceful shutdown hooks that flush KV cache; 4) a cross-platform CLI (Python) with progress bars, resumable sessions, and pipeline mode for batch embedding and rerank. Each example must include README, integration tests (smoke), and a short section describing trade-offs (latency vs batching) and recommended runtime config (batch size, cache TTL, quantization hints).
acceptance_criteria: Four runnable repos/scripts under examples/mosaic (nextjs, fastapi, go-server, cli) with README and LICENSE
Each example includes a small smoke test that runs locally and asserts streaming output and correct retry behavior
Cookbook snippets: explicit retry/backoff recipes for Python/TS/Go, streaming resume sample, and batching recommendation table
Docs include a brief production checklist: env vars, KMS hint, observability hooks, and rollout strategy
PRs created and reviewed by one SDK engineer and one platform engineer; demo recorded (5-10m)

notes: Implementation notes: emphasize small memory footprint for the Go server (use streaming encoder, avoid buffering full responses), use transparent resumable tokens for streaming (session id + last-offset), document anti-entropy: when resuming check last token hash and if mismatch, fall back to full re-request. Provide example TTLs: cache prefix 30s for chat prefix, 5m for embeddings. Include telemetry hooks (console and sample sentry/snmp integration) and a minimal cost-estimation script that runs locally to show token counts per conversation. Also include a short section on how to adapt to Dedicated: which env toggles to change (e.g., REDWOOD_ROUTE_POLICY=dedicated, REDWOOD_FALLBACK_MODEL=smaller-quantized).
